subject: Helios Health capacity validation: proposed acceptance run windows and artifacts
messages:
From: Daniel Price <d.price@helioshealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding benchmark windows + acceptance criteria

Camila —

Thanks for getting this started. We’re aiming to complete Redwood validation this week so we can flip traffic the following week. Quick context on Helios traffic: steady-state production is ~110 requests/sec (API-level calls) with 2.1 tokens per call on average; peak bursts hit ~170 req/s for ~5–10 minutes.

Acceptance criteria we need to verify during the run:
- Latency p95 < 250 ms (end-to-end at API gateway)
- Sustained throughput >= 120 req/s for 30 minutes
- Error rate (5xx) < 0.1% overall during the window
- Model output sanity: no truncation and confidence scoring within expected ranges (we’ll provide prompt sets)

Can you propose two run windows (one daytime, one evening) and confirm the artifacts you will share (raw logs, per-route latency CSV, and a Redwood run config)? Also confirm what environment you’ll use (hosted vs dedicated) and any expected pre-warm steps.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Price
Director, Platform Reliability
Helios Health

Thanks — here’s a short plan we can execute and the artifacts we’ll produce. Attaching the detailed load plan (spreadsheet) and the redwood_run_config we’ll feed into our harness.

Proposed windows (PT):
- Option A (day): Thu, 2027-05-13 09:30–11:00 PT (ramp to 130 req/s, hold 30min)
- Option B (evening): Thu, 2027-05-13 20:00–21:30 PT (ramp to 150 req/s, two 15-min holds)

What we will run and share:
- Environment: Dedicated pool (m5d cased GPU profile) — we recommend dedicated for acceptance to get predictable throughput and exact reproducibility.
- Pre-warm: 10-min warmup at 40% expected throughput + KV cache priming with your canonical prompt set.
- Ramp schedule: 0 -> 50 -> 90 -> target over 12 minutes, then hold for the acceptance window.
- Artifacts: raw request logs (gzipped), per-request latency CSV, aggregated per-second throughput, Redwood run config (JSON), and model output samples for the verification prompt set.
- Sanity checks: token counts, output length distribution, and confidence score flags.

Attachments: 20270512_helios_load_plan.xlsx (load/traffic matrix), redwood_run_config_v2.json (harness settings).

Next steps: please confirm Option A or B and whether you want an extra late-evening run. Once confirmed we’ll loop in our infra lead (rishi) to provision the pool and dev (cc’d) to set up the run artifacts and S3 delivery.

Camila / team —

We can provision the dedicated pool for Option A. Quick notes from infra:
- Recommended nodes: 2 x A100-40GB equivalent to achieve baseline 120 req/s with batching=auto; reserve 1 extra node for autoscale to 4 during burst validation.
- Quant/Model: will run float16 + 4-bit activation quant profile for cost while preserving latency. Expect ~15–20% extra CPU overhead on tokenization side (affects end-to-end).
- KV cache: will seed top-1k canonical prompts; this reduces cold-start tail latency. Please attach the prompt set to the run config.
- Tracing: adding trace-id at request-level is done; our logs will include trace_id, request_id, and model_latency_ms.
- Ramp: we’ll do the 12-minute ramp Camila suggested. For safety we’ll cap aggressive bursts at 150 req/s for short holds only.

I’ll create the run infra ticket (ONB-3421) and push the image tag + node sizes to the shared Drive link. Will also coordinate with Dev for S3 manifests.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
